desc: Implement helper `cost(num, t)`: returns the smallest non-negative increment such that `num + inc` is a multiple of `t`, i.e. `((t - num % t) % t)`.
Build a DP table `dp[mask][i]` where `mask` is a bitmask over targets (size `T ≤ 4`) and `i` indexes `nums`. Initialize `dp[0][i] = 0` for all `i` (no targets assigned, zero cost).
Iterate over masks and indices; for each, transition to adding any uncovered target `j` to the current `nums[i]`, updating `dp[mask | (1<<j)][i]`.
Handle "skip element i" transitions so the DP can leave some `nums` unused.
The final answer is the minimum of `dp[(1<<T)-1][i]` over all `i` (all targets covered, using any subset of elements).
Test the implementation against the provided examples (3 cases) and ensure outputs are 1, 2, 0 respectively.
Verify handling of edge cases: target already satisfied, duplicate target values, n=1, T=1.
Correct the DP to allow a single `nums[i]` to cover a non-empty subset of targets (using LCM and next-multiple cost) rather than only one target.
Final solution uses DP over subsets of `nums` with state representing which targets are satisfied, allowing each `nums[i]` to be incremented to cover any subset of remaining targets.
